sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SPLIT-FLOW PATTERN IN MID-UPPER LEVELS FEATURES CYCLONE INITIALLY LOCATED OVER CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS...FCST TO MOVE EWD ACROSS KS TO WRN MO BY 25/00Z AND WEAKEN ALONG WITH ITS SFC MANIFESTATION. MEANWHILE...STG SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND SPEED MAX ALOFT -- WHICH COMPRISED MOST OF INITIAL UPPER CYCLONE OVER SWRN CONUS DURING PREVIOUS FEW DAYS -- IS FCST TO EJECT NEWD FROM CENTRAL TX TO ERN MO/SRN IL AREA BY 25/00Z...TAKING OVER AGAIN AS PRIMARY 500 MB LOW. BY THAT TIME...CORRESPONDING SFC CYCLONE WILL FORM ALONG OCCLUSION TRIPLE POINT E OF ORIGINAL...AND CLOSE TO NEWER MID-UPPER CYCLONE CENTER. THIS PROCESS WILL RESULT IN REINFORCEMENT/ACCELERATION OF INITIALLY STALLED FRONTAL SEGMENT NOW OVER SWRN/CENTRAL TX NNEWD OVER ERN OK. FRONT SHOULD MOVE ACROSS MUCH OF LA...WRN MS AND WRN PORTIONS TN/KY BY 25/00Z...TO FL PANHANDLE...AL...MIDDLE-ERN TN AND ERN KY BY END OF PERIOD....WHEN MID-UPPER CYCLONE SHOULD BE OVER NRN PORTIONS IL/INDIANA...AND SRN LM AREA.

sections.title: LOWER MS VALLEY...MID-SOUTH AND TN VALLEY REGIONS
sections.text: TSTMS SHOULD BE INCREASING IN COVERAGE/INTENSITY AROUND BEGINNING OF PERIOD OVER E TX...LA AND ARKLATEX REGION. FOREGOING AIR MASS -- ALREADY MOISTENED/DESTABILIZED FAVORABLY BY PRIOR/OVERNIGHT THETAE ADVECTION...WILL FURTHER DESTABILIZE AMIDST SFC DIABATIC HEATING. AMOUNT OF HEATING IS SOMEWHAT IN QUESTION BECAUSE OF POTENTIAL FOR CLOUD/ANVIL DEBRIS SPREADING DOWNSTREAM IN MID-UPPER LEVELS FROM EARLY CONVECTION...PERHAPS INCLUDING TEMPORAL EXTENSION OF ACTIVITY NOW OVER S TX. STILL...AWAY FROM EXISTING CONVECTION...EVERY REASONABLE SCENARIO INDICATES THAT MLCINH GENERALLY WILL WEAKEN WITH NWD EXTENT FROM GULF COAST...SUPPORTING EARLY AND RAPID DEVELOPMENT AND INTENSIFICATION OF TSTMS FROM MID-MORNING THROUGH MID-AFTERNOON...AND SUSTAINED THREAT SHIFTING EWD AND NEWD ACROSS OUTLOOK AREA INTO EVENING/OVERNIGHT HOURS. INTENSE VERTICAL WIND PROFILES WILL SPREAD ACROSS BROAD WARM/MOIST SECTOR TODAY...MUCH OF WHICH ALREADY IS IN PLACE ACROSS MUCH OF LA...MS AND COASTAL AL. THIS AIR MASS WILL SPREAD INLAND TOWARD TN VALLEY AS CONVECTION/PRECIP NOW OVER TN/AL/GA SHIFTS NEWD. SFC DEW POINTS WILL BE 70S INVOF GULF COAST...TRANSITIONING TO UPPER 60S AS FAR N AS TN AND LOW-MID 60S TO OH VALLE

sections.title: IA...MO VALLEY REGION
sections.text: SCATTERED STG-SVR TSTMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ACROSS THIS AREA INVOF LARGE CYCLONE ALOFT...AS STEEP MID-UPPER LEVEL LAPSE RATES COLLOCATED WITH BROAD AREA OF LOW-LEVEL CONVERGENCE AND DIABATIC/DIURNAL DESTABILIZATION OF BOUNDARY LAYER. MAIN CONCERN WILL BE SVR HAIL...THOUGH POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING GUSTS EXISTS. SVR POTENTIAL SHOULD WANE SIGNIFICANTLY AFTER SUNSET. ..EDWARDS/GARNER.. 04/24/2010

sections.title: LA/MS/AL/TN
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE BEEN INCREASING IN COVERAGE AND INTENSITY THIS MORNING ACROSS PARTS OF LA/AR/MS...ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE PRIMARY SURFACE COLD FRONT. RAPIDLY STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL WINDS AND WARM ADVECTION ARE LEADING TO DISCRETE CONVECTIVE INITIATION...WITH NUMEROUS STORMS SHOWING MID LEVEL ROTATION. THIS ACTIVITY WILL SPREAD EASTWARD INTO AL AND TN WITH THE POTENTIAL FOR LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND TORNADOES THROUGH THE MORNING. A FEW HOURS OF HEATING WILL LIKELY PROMOTE ANOTHER ROUND OF SEVERE STORMS BY EARLY AFTERNOON OVER EASTERN MS...MUCH OF AL...AND POTENTIALLY INTO MIDDLE TN. THESE STORMS ARE FORECAST TO BE THE MORE SIGNIFICANT OF THIS EVENT...WITH THE RISK OF DAMAGING TORNADOES AND WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS. STORMS WILL TRACK EASTWARD INTO WESTERN GA DURING THE EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: MID MS AND LOWER OH VALLEYS
sections.text: ALL MODEL GUIDANCE AGREES ON RAPID SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS OVER PARTS OF MO/IL BY EARLY AFTERNOON AS THE EXIT REGION OF A 90+ KNOT MID LEVEL SPEED MAX NOSES INTO THE AREA. STRONG SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS WILL TRANSPORT MOISTURE NORTHWARD AND HELP TO DESTABILIZE PARTS OF MO/IL/IND/KY AHEAD OF THE SURFACE LOW. FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST VERTICAL SHEAR AND CAPE PROFILES QUITE FAVORABLE FOR TORNADIC SUPERCELLS DURING THE AFTERNOON. THE MAIN FORECAST QUESTION IN THIS AREA INVOLVES THE EVOLUTION OF CONVECTION FARTHER SOUTH AND WHETHER IT WILL IMPEDE MOISTURE RETURN THROUGH THE DAY. ..HART/SMITH.. 04/24/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: WATER VAPOR IMAGERY REFLECTS A NEUTRAL TO INCREASINGLY NEGATIVE TILT/VIGOROUS SHORTWAVE TROUGH ACROSS THE CENTRAL/SOUTHERN PLAINS...WITH AN ATTENDANT 130+ KT UPPER JET STREAK SURGING NORTHEASTWARD ALONG THE TX COAST AS OF 12Z. THESE FEATURES WILL CONTINUE TO SHIFT EAST-NORTHEASTWARD TODAY TOWARD THE MS RIVER VALLEY....AND RESULT IN WIDESPREAD INTENSE THUNDERSTORMS WITH ALL SEVERE STORM MODES/RISKS PROBABLE INTO TONIGHT.

sections.title: MS/AL/TN/KY/FAR NORTHEAST AR/MO BOOTHEEL
sections.text: HAVE EXPANDED CATEGORICAL HIGH RISK NORTHWARD ACROSS PORTIONS OF WESTERN TN/WESTERN KY. UPPER 60S F/LOWER 70S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS ARE IN PLACE WITHIN A PRISTINE WARM/MOIST SECTOR ALONG/SOUTH OF A WARM FRONT...WHICH IS EXPECTED TO CONTINUE TO RETREAT NORTHWARD ACROSS THE CENTRAL GULF COAST STATES/TN VALLEY INTO THIS EVENING. RAPIDLY STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL WINDS AND WARM ADVECTION WILL CONTINUE TO LEAD TO SEMI-DISCRETE CONVECTIVE SUPERCELLULAR INITIATION...WITH MORE OF A MIXED SUPERCELLULAR/QUASI-LINEAR MODE PROBABLE NORTHWARD TOWARD THE OH/MS RIVER CONFLUENCE. STRONG/ELONGATED LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPHS WILL SUPPORT THE POSSIBILITY OF STRONG AND DAMAGING TORNADOES...ALONG WITH DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL.

sections.title: LOWER OH VALLEY
sections.text: LOWER 60S F SURFACE DEWPOINTS ARE WELL ESTABLISHED AS FAR NORTH OF THE MIDDLE MS/LOWER OH RIVER VALLEYS ALONG/SOUTH OF A RESIDUAL QUASI-STATIONARY/WARM FRONT. SIMILAR TO OBSERVATIONAL TRENDS...ALL MODEL GUIDANCE AGREES ON RAPID SURFACE CYCLOGENESIS NORTHEASTWARD INTO PARTS OF MO/IL THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AS THE EXIT REGION OF A 90+ KNOT MID LEVEL SPEED MAX NOSES INTO THE AREA. STRONG SOUTHEASTERLY LOW LEVEL WINDS WILL TRANSPORT MOISTURE NORTHWARD AND HELP TO DESTABILIZE PARTS OF MO/IL/IND AHEAD OF THE DEEPENING SURFACE LOW. WITH A MIXED MODE OF QUASI-DISCRETE SUPERCELLS AND EVENTUAL QLCS DEVELOPMENT...FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST VERTICAL SHEAR AND CAPE PROFILES QUITE FAVORABLE FOR TORNADIC SUPERCELLS/DAMAGING WINDS INTO THIS EVENING.

sections.title: LOWER/MIDDLE MO RIVER VALLEY THROUGH AFTERNOON
sections.text: OTHER LOWER-TOPPED SEVERE STORMS...WITH A RISK OF SEVERE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO...WILL EXIST FARTHER WEST ACROSS PORTIONS OF THE MIDWEST TO MO RIVER VALLEY. THIS RISK WILL BE ROUGHLY FOCUSED ALONG SURFACE OCCLUSION AND BENEATH VERTICALLY STACKED UPPER LOW. ANY SEVERE RISK ACROSS THIS REGION SHOULD RAPIDLY WANE AFTER DARK. ..GUYER/GRAMS.. 04/24/2010

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: SPLIT-FLOW PATTERN PREVAILS OVER CENTRAL NORTH AMERICA...FEATURING BROAD MID-UPPER LEVEL CYCLONE THAT IS MOVING/REDEVELOPING EWD FROM CENTRAL PLAINS TO MID MS VALLEY. STG SHORTWAVE TROUGH...THAT HAD BEEN PRIMARY COMPONENT OF ORIGINAL UPPER CYCLONE A FEW DAYS AGO OVER CA/NV...IS MOVING NEWD ACROSS SRN/ERN MO AND WILL BECOME PRIMARY CYCLONE CENTER AGAIN SHORTLY. RESULTING 500 MB LOW WILL MOVE NEWD ACROSS IL THROUGH REMAINDER PERIOD...BECOMING VERTICALLY STACKED WITH DEEP SFC CYCLONE NOW ANALYZED AT 23Z NNW STL. LEADING COLD FRONT...WHICH ALSO IS ACTING EFFECTIVELY AS DRYLINE...WAS ANALYZED AT 23Z FROM SWRN IL SSEWD ACROSS NERN MS...SWWD TO JUST E JAN...NEAR BTR THEN OFFSHORE LA. SECONDARY COLD FRONT WAS EVIDENT OVER SERN MO...CENTRAL AR AND NE TX. LEADING BOUNDARY IS EXPECTED TO REACH WRN/CENTRAL FL PANHANDLE...SERN AL...NWRN GA...ERN TN...AND CENTRAL/ERN KY BY END OF PERIOD.

sections.title: MID MS VALLEY TO TN AND OH VALLEY REGIONS AND CENTRAL AL
sections.text: REMAINDER OF ONGOING SVR OUTBREAK FCST TO SHIFT EWD ACROSS THIS REGION IN FORM OF SEVERAL BANDS AND CLUSTERS. FOR NEAR-TERM POTENTIAL...REF SPC WWS 96-99 AND RELATED MESOSCALE DISCUSSIONS. ALTHOUGH SVR HAZARD OVERALL IS NOT AS EXTREME AS EARLIER TODAY...GIVEN GRADUAL DIMINISHMENT/DISPLACEMENT OF OPTIMAL INSTABILITY/SHEAR COMBINATIONS...SOME POTENTIAL FOR STRONG/DAMAGING TORNADOES WILL PERSIST PRIMARILY FROM MIDDLE-ERN TN SWD THROUGH PORTIONS AL...AND PERHAPS SOME OF WRN GA. MOSTLY QUASI-LINEAR MODES WITH A FEW DISCRETE SUPERCELLS ARE POSSIBLE FARTHER N ACROSS OH...NRN KY...IL AND INDIANA. SVR WIND ALSO IS DISTINCT THREAT...ESPECIALLY FROM BOWS SUCH AS THAT OBSERVED ATTM OVER ERN KY MOVING INTO AT LEAST MARGINALLY SFC-BASED INFLOW. AIR MASS IS EXPECTED TO DESTABILIZE BEHIND ONGOING/ELEVATED CONVECTION OVER ERN AL AND GA...WITHING REGIME OF STG LOW-LEVEL THETAE ADVECTION. SHIFTING OF STRONGEST ISALLOBARIC FORCING AWAY FROM THIS REGION WILL LEAD TO SOME VEERING OF SFC WINDS. HOWEVER...MAINTENANCE OF SOME HODOGRAPH CURVATURE WITH LARGE 0-1 KM SRH AND SPEED SHEAR WILL PERSIST THROUGH THIS EVENING AND INTO TONIGHT...AS LLJ ONLY GRADUALLY SHIFTS EWD AND WEAKENS FROM 60 KT 40 KT...AND AS M

sections.title: OVERNIGHT -- GULF COAST
sections.text: BAND OF TSTMS IS FCST ACROSS THIS REGION LATER TONIGHT NEAR FRONT...BACKBUILDING SWD OVER GULF. THIS MAY BE CONTINUATION OF ONGOING ACTIVITY OR NEWER/ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT. LOW-LEVEL FLOW FCST TO VEER OVERNIGHT JUST AHEAD OF SFC FRONT OVER AL...WRN FL PANHANDLE EWD TO SWRN GA AND CENTRAL FL PANHANDLE. THIS WILL RESULT IN FAVORABLY RICH THETAE AND DEEPENING BOUNDARY LAYER TO COMBINE WITH AT LEAST MARGINALLY SUPPORTIVE LOW LEVEL CONVERGENCE IN WEAKENING CINH EVIDENT IN 21Z TLH/ATL AREA RAOBS. THIS TREND ALREADY IS EVIDENT WHEN COMPARING 21Z/00Z TLH SOUNDINGS...WHICH ALSO MAINTAINED ENLARGED LOW-LEVEL HODOGRAPHS. AFTER ABOUT 06Z....EXPECT MORE UNIDIRECTIONAL DEEP-LAYER WINDS AND RELATED KINEMATIC SUPPORT FOR DOMINANT QUASI-LINEAR MODE. DAMAGING GUSTS ARE POSSIBLE...ALONG WITH CONDITIONAL TORNADO POTENTIAL LINGERING GIVEN PRESENCE OF EMBEDDED SUPERCELLS OR BOW/LEWP MESOCIRCULATIONS. ..EDWARDS.. 04/25/2010
